subject: Throughput targets and network handshake for Helio private pool
messages:
From: Balraj Singh <ops@helio.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: network-sre@helio.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private pool throughput targets + egress constraints (Helio)

Hi Hannah/Laura,

Thanks for the initial intake earlier this week. We need a one-page capacity target for the private GPU pool Redwood will run in our VPC so we can align procurement and the colo team. High-level asks:

- Target sustained throughput: 1200 qps (50-token average gen) with p95 latency <= 200ms.
- Burst envelope: short spikes up to 4k qps for up to 10 minutes/day.
- Egress: our peering has a 10 Gbps cap to the Redwood subnet but NAT throughput to public endpoints is limited to 4 Gbps; please call out any implications.
- Routing: prefer multi-AZ failover; we run in us-west-2 primary.

Can you send a short note with assumptions (model family, batching, KV cache hit, GPU count+type, expected warm pool) and any network changes we should request? We also attached a simple traffic sample (see helio-egress-matrix.pdf).

Best,
Balraj
Ops Lead, Helio Systems

Attachments: helio-egress-matrix.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Balraj Singh <ops@helio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool throughput targets + egress constraints (Helio)

Balraj — thanks, this is clear and a good starting point. Quick summary of what we'll produce in the next 24 hours:

1) A capacity sketch with two sizing options: "predictable" (reserved: higher GPUs, lower amortized latency) and "elastic" (autoscale + warm pool tradeoffs).
2) Network constraints section showing where the 4 Gbps NAT cap matters and recommended peering changes.
3) Runbook bullets for warm cache population, admission control thresholds and canary failover behavior across AZs.

Assumptions we plan to use — please flag any that don't match Helio's expectations:
- Model: a 7B decoder-only family (opt/llama-style) with 50-token avg output and 64-token total window for scheduling math.
- KV cache hit: 40% effective hit on repeated sessions.
- Batch target: 8 request-level batching (continuous batching) for sustained flow; bursts will rely on pre-warmed pods.
- GPU type: A100-equivalent (80GB) as baseline; we'll also show M60-like cheaper quantized variants.
- Warm pool: keep ~10% of estimated sustained pods warm to handle 2x sustained traffic with coldstart amortization.

Jonas — can you run the rough GPU->qps math and call out the egress token bandwidth given 50 tokens/output? I want a slim PDF and the XLS with the model math.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — hannah@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Balraj Singh <ops@helio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool throughput targets + egress constraints (Helio)

Balraj / Hannah — attached is the spreadsheet (helio_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with the back-of-envelope. Key points from the calc:

- Baseline throughput per GPU (A100-eq): ~160 qps sustained for 50-token avg generation at 64-window, single-model instance, with continuous batching level ~8 and CPU+NVMe not bottlenecking. That yields ~8 GPUs to reach 1200 qps sustained (1200 / 160 = 7.5 -> round to 8).
- Burst plan: to handle 4k qps for short windows we recommend a warm-pool of 18 GPUs (8 baseline + 10 warm) or an autoscaling headroom to 24 GPUs if you prefer headroom for model variants and quantization slowdowns.
- Latency: with 8 GPUs and continuous batching we estimate p95 compute latency ~120-160ms; network/serialization headroom adds ~20-40ms depending on AZ cross-talk.
- Egress bandwidth: 50 tokens * 1.1 bytes/token (compression+headers) * 1200 qps ~ 66 KB/s per qps -> ~79 MB/s total -> ~0.63 Gbps for sustained 1200 qps. For 4k qps bursts this scales to ~2.5 Gbps. That stays under the 4 Gbps NAT cap for bursts, but remember add control-plane, telemetry, and any artifacts (model downloads) to reserve ~0.5 Gbps. Peak with autoscaling headroom to 24 GPUs could push transient egress near 3.5 Gbps; still under 4 Gbps but tight.

Network recommendations included in the sheet:
- Increase NAT throughput to 6 Gbps or enable a dedicated peer path for token egress (private peering to Redwood compute-on-VPC) to avoid NAT bottleneck.
- Ensure peering to our management plane is multi-AZ with at least 10 Gbps interconnect to avoid cross-AZ latency spikes.

Operational notes:
- Warm cache: target popular prefixes and session affinity so effective KV hit >40% during morning rush.
- Admission control: set soft throttle at 1,800 qps cluster-level and hard at 4,000 qps to match burst envelope with graceful degradation to a smaller model.

I've attached the XLS and a 2-page summary PDF in the Drive link Hannah will share. Let me know if you'd like the math parametrized for a smaller 4-bit quantized model — that changes GPU qps by ~x1.6.

— Jonas
Senior Capacity Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: helio_capacity_model_v1.xlsx
From: Balraj Singh <ops@helio.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private pool throughput targets + egress constraints (Helio)

Thanks, team — that aligns with our internal expectations. Two quick follow-ups:

1) We'll open a request with colo to upgrade NAT throughput to 6 Gbps and confirm multi-AZ peering; expect a ticket by end of day Monday.
2) Can you add a short section in the summary that maps out "what to expect" during an autoscale event (steps, expected time-to-scale, and how KV warmup reduces token load over the first 3 minutes)? That will help our SRE runbook.

If you can drop a 1-page appendix with those bullets and the Drive link to the XLS, we can lock procurement numbers next week.

Appreciate the quick turn — Balraj
Ops Lead, Helio Systems
